problems.title: Reduce a squared logarithm to a quadratic
problems.question: Solve $[\log_4(4x+4)]^2+\log_4((x+1)^2)=13$.
steps: Then (t+1)²+2t=13, giving t²+4t−12=(t−2)(t+6)=0.
Both satisfy x>−1.

problems.title: A cone net and volume determine its radius
problems.question: A cone’s net is a 216° sector and its volume is 96π. Find the base radius.
problems.idea: Compare the sector arc with the base circumference.
steps: Write r=3k,l=5k,h=4k.
Volume=π·9k²·4k/3=12πk³=96π, so k=2.
Thus r=6.

problems.title: A quotient of logarithms
problems.question: Solve log₉(3x²)/log₉x≥4.
steps: The inequality becomes 2+1/(2t)≥4, or 1/(2t)≥2.
For t<0 it fails. For t>0 it gives t≤1/4.
Thus 0<log₉x≤1/4.

problems.title: Investigate a rational function completely
problems.question: Investigate and sketch y=(3x²+2x−1)/(3x+1): domain, range, monotonicity, concavity, critical points and asymptotes.
problems.idea: Divide first, then differentiate the simple form.
steps: Domain: all real x except −1/3. Vertical asymptote: x=−1/3; slant asymptote: y=x+1/3.
f′>0 on both domain intervals, so both branches increase and there are no stationary extrema.
f″>0 to the left of −1/3 and f″<0 to the right. The break is not an inflection point because it is outside the domain.
The x-intercepts are −1 and 1/3; the y-intercept is −1.
As x→−∞, f→−∞; as x→(−1/3)−, f→+∞. On the right branch the limits are −∞ at the asymptote and +∞ at +∞. Hence the range is all real numbers.
problems.answer: Two increasing branches; domain R excluding −1/3; range R; asymptotes x=−1/3 and y=x+1/3.

problems.title: Two circles from an unspecified hyperbola focus
problems.question: Find a circle through a focus of (x+1)²/4−(y−3)²/9=1 and both foci of (x−1)²/9+(y−4)²/4=1.
problems.idea: There are two hyperbola foci, so check both.
formulas: Hyperbola foci H±=(−1±√13,3); ellipse foci E±=(1±√5,4).
steps: Any circle through both E± has centre (1,k), on their perpendicular bisector, and radius squared 5+(4−k)².
Requiring H± to lie on the circle gives (−2±√13)²+(3−k)²=5+(4−k)².
Simplification gives k=−5/2±2√13, with the corresponding sign.
Thus there are two circles, one for each choice of hyperbola focus.
problems.note: The source does not specify which hyperbola focus, so both circles must be retained.

problems.title: Two integrals with different substitutions
problems.question: Evaluate (a) $\int\sqrt x\sin(x\sqrt x)\,dx$; (b) $\int_0^\pi(\sin x+|\sin x|)\,dx$.
problems.idea: Use u=x√x in the first and the sine sign in the second.
steps: (a) The integral becomes (2/3)∫sin u du=−(2/3)cos u+C.
(b) The integrand is 2sin x, whose integral from 0 to π is 4.

problems.title: Angle between two spatial lines
problems.question: Find the acute angle between the line given by 2x+y−3z−1=0, x+y−4=0, and the line (2x−1)/3=(4−y)/5=z−3.
problems.idea: Get a direction vector for each line.
formulas: The first direction is (2,1,−3)×(1,1,0)=(3,−3,1). The second may be (3,−10,2).
steps: Their dot product is 41 and squared lengths are 19 and 113.
Use the absolute dot product divided by the lengths.

problems.title: Largest cyclic trapezoid with one fixed base
problems.question: A trapezoid is inscribed in a circle of radius R, the centre lies inside it, and one base has length R√3. Find a leg of the maximum-area trapezoid.
problems.idea: Every cyclic trapezoid is isosceles. Optimize the position of its other base.
formulas: The fixed chord is distance R/2 from the centre. Put the opposite chord at distance tR on the other side, 0<t<1.
steps: The area is F(t)=R²(√3+2√(1−t²))(1/2+t)/2.
Its derivative divided by R² is √3/2+[1−2t²−t/2]/√(1−t²). This derivative decreases strictly for t≥0, so there is at most one maximum.
Substitution t=cos40° gives zero, using the triple-angle relation cos120°=−1/2. The derivative is positive at t=0 and negative near 1, so this is the maximum.
The fixed base subtends 120°; the remaining 240° arc is divided into three equal 80° arcs in this configuration. Each leg is the chord of an 80° arc.

problems.title: Distance to a section plane in a rectangular box
problems.question: A box has AB=2,BC=4,AA₁=6. M is the midpoint of CD. Find the distance from C₁ to the plane through A,B₁,M.
problems.idea: Use coordinates and a plane normal.
steps: B₁×M=(−24,6,8), so a simplified plane equation is −12x+3y+4z=0.
At C₁ the left side is −24+12+24=12. The normal length is √169=13.

problems.title: A global monotonicity condition becomes a quadratic in cosine
problems.question: Find every a for which f(x)=(1/3)sin³x−sin x(a+cos x)+(1−2a)x−2 decreases on all real numbers.
steps: The first factor is always positive.
The second factor is at most zero for every c exactly when a≥1, because its maximum at c=0 is 1−a.
For a=1 the derivative is negative except at isolated zeros, so f is still strictly decreasing.
